## Zero(es)/Root(s) of Quadratic Equation
A real number <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>α</mi></mrow></math> is said to be a root of the quadratic equation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, if <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>α</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>.
The zeroes of the quadratic polynomial <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></math> and the roots of the equation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> are same.
QUADRATIC EQUATIONS
## Relation Between Zeroes and Coefficient of a Quadratic Equation
If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>α</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>β</mi></mrow></math> are zeroes of the quadratic equation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></math> are real numbers and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, then
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>&</mi><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mspace linebreak="newline" /><mi>&</mi><mo>⇒</mo><mtext> sum of zeroes </mtext><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mtext> coefficient of </mtext><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mtext> coefficient of </mtext><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac><mspace linebreak="newline" /><mi>&</mi><mi>α</mi><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mspace linebreak="newline" /><mi>&</mi><mo>⇒</mo><mtext> product of zeroes </mtext><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mtext> constant term </mtext></mrow><mrow><mtext> coefficient of </mtext><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow></math>
Quadratic Equation:
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>α</mi><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>.
## QUADRATIC EQUATIONS
A polynomial of any variable <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> of degree two in standard form <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, when equated to zero is called a Quadratic Equation of variable <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math>. [In standard form of quadratic polynomial, the power of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> are in descending order.] Thus, standard form of a Quadratic Equation of variable <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>; where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></math> all are real numbers but <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>. Here ' <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></math> ' and ' <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow></math> ' are called coefficient of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> respectively. ' <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow></math> ' is called constant term.
The term "quadratic" comes from the Latin word "quadratus" which mean square. Know
## STANDARD FORM OF A QUADRATIC EQUATION
In the standard form of a quadratic equation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>,
(i) all the terms (except zero) are in one side of equal sign <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and zero <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> is in other side of equal sign.
(ii) the power of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> are in descending order.
(iii) either or both ' <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow></math> ' and ' <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow></math> ' can be equal to zero but <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>. Therefore, a quadratic equation may be in the form of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> or <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>.
(iv) the term of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> (i.e. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ), term of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> (i.e. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> ) or constant term (i.e. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow></math> ) can not be more than one.
If not so, then by adding/subtracting the like terms or taking the common factor from like terms, we convert the quadratic equation in the standard form, in which there is not more than one term of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> and constant term.
For example: Standard form of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>
Standard form of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msqrt><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>.
Note : Sometimes there are two or more constant terms which can not be added/subtracted or have no any common factor, then both the constant terms are put in to a bracket so that all constant terms become a single constant term.
For example: Standard form of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msqrt><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msqrt><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>
## SOLUTION :
(i) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>⇒</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>
This is a polynomial of degree 3 , therefore it is not quadratic equation.
(ii) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> is not a quadratic equation because it contains a term involving <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.
(iii) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>⇒</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>
This is the quadratic equation.
## SOLUTION OR ROOTS OF A QUADRATIC EQUATION
The values of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> which satisfy the given quadratic equation are called solutions/roots of the given quadratic equation.
For example if <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></math> is one of solutions of the quadratic equation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>α</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>.
A quadratic equation has either two real roots or two not real roots. The two real roots may be equal or different.
To find the solutions (or to find the roots) of a quadratic equation, first we check whether the given quadratic equation is in standard form or not. If not, then first convert the given quadratic equation in standard form, then by using any of the following given three methods, you can solve the given quadratic equation.
Note: A quadratic equation has always two solutions/roots (i.e., two value of the variable ' <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> ' always satisfy the quadratic equation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> )
## SOLUTION :
(i) L.H.S : <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msqrt><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></math>, Put <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msqrt></mrow></math>, L.H.S <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msqrt><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>=</mo></mrow></math> R.H.S.
Put <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msqrt></mrow></math>, L.H.S. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msqrt><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>=</mo></mrow></math> R.H.S. So, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msqrt></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msqrt></mrow></math> are the solutions
(ii) L.H.S. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>, Put <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>, L.H.S. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>≠</mo></mrow></math> R.H.S. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mspace width="1em" /><mo>∴</mo><mspace width="1em" /><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> is not a solution Put <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>, L.H.S. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>≠</mo></mrow></math> R.H.S.
## Method I : Solution of a Quadratic Equation by Factorisation
Quadratic equation : <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>
By spliting the middle term ' <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> ' of L.H.S, factorise the L.H.S <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> into linear factors. Then after equating each factor to zero, we find the values of the variable ' <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> ' of the quadratic equation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>.
These value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> are the solutions/roots of the given quadratic equation.

(ii) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>9</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mn>9</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>⇒</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> or <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> or <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>

## NATURE OF ROOTS
For the quadratic equation: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> is called discriminant of the quadratic equation. The value of ( <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></math> ) is denoted by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>D</mi></mrow></math>.
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∴</mo><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></math>
The discriminant plays an important role in finding the nature of the roots of the quadratic equation.
(i) If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, then roots are real and equal.
(ii) If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, then roots are real and unequal.
(iii) If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, then roots are not real.

If one pipe takes 3 minutes more than the other to fill it, find the time in which each pipe would fill the cistern.
Sol. Let the faster pipe takes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> minutes to fill the cistern. Therefore, the slower pipe will take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> minutes to fill the cistern.
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∴</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>40</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>13</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>40</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>13</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mn>13</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>41</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>120</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>13</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>24</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> or <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>24</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>13</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>⇒</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mspace width="1em" /><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mo>∵</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></math>

## SEQUENCE
The number patterns or arrangement of numbers according to definite rule or a set of rules is called a SEQUENCE.
The various numbers occuring in a sequence are called its terms. The <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term of the sequence is denoted by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math>. The <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term is also called the GENERAL TERM of the sequence. For example,
(i) The numbers <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>⟨</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi></mrow></math>.<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>⟩</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>q</mi><mi>u</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>w</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>h</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>u</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>𝐍</mi></mrow></math>.
(ii) The numbers <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">⟨</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow></math> represent a sequence written according to the rule <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>𝐍</mi></mrow></math>.
(iii) The numbers <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>⟨</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi></mrow></math>.<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>⟩</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>q</mi><mi>u</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>w</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>h</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>u</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>𝐍</mi></mrow></math>.
(iv) The numbers <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>⟨</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>13</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>21</mn><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>⟩</mi></mrow></math> represent a sequence written according to the rule <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>𝐍</mi></mrow></math>.
(v) The numbers <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>⟨</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi></mrow></math>.<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>⟩</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>q</mi><mi>u</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>w</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>h</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>f</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>f</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>u</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>s</mi><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>></mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>𝐍</mi></mrow></math>. This sequence of numbers is called the Fibonacci sequence.
(vi) The numbers <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>⟨</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>13</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo></mrow></math>. represent a sequence of prime numbers.
Note that in every sequence it is not always possible to write a specific formula.
## METHODS OF DESCRIBING A SEQUENCE
(i) A sequence may be described by writing first few terms till the rule for writing down the other terms is evident.
(ii) A sequence may be described by giving a formula for its general term (the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term).
(iii) A sequence may be described by specifying first few terms and a formula (or a set of formulae) giving a relation between successive terms. Such a formula is called RECURSIVE FORMULA (or RECURRENCE RELATION).
(iv) Some sequences may not be described by any rule.
## SERIES
If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">⟨</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow></math> is a sequence, then the expression <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>…</mi></mrow></math>. is called the series associated with the given sequence.
## PROGRESSION
A sequence is said to be a PROGRESSION if its terms numerically increase or numerically decrease continuously.

## QUADRATIC EQUATIONS
A polynomial of any variable <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> of degree two in standard form <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, when equated to zero is called a Quadratic Equation of variable <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math>. ' <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow></math> ' is called constant term.

theory_sections.topics: STANDARD FORM OF A QUADRATIC EQUATION
theory_sections.markdown:
## STANDARD FORM OF A QUADRATIC EQUATION
In the standard form of a quadratic equation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>,
(i) all the terms (except zero) are in one side of equal sign <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and zero <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> is in other side of equal sign.
(ii) the power of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> are in descending order.
(iii) either or both ' <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow></math> ' and ' <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow></math> ' can be equal to zero but <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>. Therefore, a quadratic equation may be in the form of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> or <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>.
(iv) the term of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> (i.e. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ), term of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> (i.e. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> ) or constant term (i.e. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow></math> ) can not be more than one.
If not so, then by adding/subtracting the like terms or taking the common factor from like terms, we convert the quadratic equation in the standard form, in which there is not more than one term of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> and constant term.
For example: Standard form of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>
Standard form of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msqrt><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>.
Note : Sometimes there are two or more constant terms which can not be added/subtracted or have no any common factor, then both the constant terms are put in to a bracket so that all constant terms become a single constant term.
For example: Standard form of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msqrt><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msqrt><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>

theory_sections.topics: SOLUTION OR ROOTS OF A QUADRATIC EQUATION
theory_sections.markdown:
## SOLUTION OR ROOTS OF A QUADRATIC EQUATION
The values of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> which satisfy the given quadratic equation are called solutions/roots of the given quadratic equation.
For example if <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></math> is one of solutions of the quadratic equation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>α</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>.
A quadratic equation has either two real roots or two not real roots. The two real roots may be equal or different.
To find the solutions (or to find the roots) of a quadratic equation, first we check whether the given quadratic equation is in standard form or not. If not, then first convert the given quadratic equation in standard form, then by using any of the following given three methods, you can solve the given quadratic equation.
Note: A quadratic equation has always two solutions/roots (i.e., two value of the variable ' <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> ' always satisfy the quadratic equation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> )

theory_sections.topics: Method I : Solution of a Quadratic Equation by Factorisation
theory_sections.markdown:
## Method I : Solution of a Quadratic Equation by Factorisation
Quadratic equation : <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>
By spliting the middle term ' <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> ' of L.H.S, factorise the L.H.S <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> into linear factors. Then after equating each factor to zero, we find the values of the variable ' <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> ' of the quadratic equation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>.
These value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> are the solutions/roots of the given quadratic equation.

## Special Cases
Standard from of the quadratic equation : <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>
(i) If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>⇒</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>⇒</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>
(ii) If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>⇒</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mo>⇒</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>±</mi><msqrt><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></msqrt></mrow></math>
(iii) If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>⇒</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>⇒</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>

## For examples:
(a) If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>5</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>. Hence, solutions: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>
(b) If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, then solution : <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>±</mi><msqrt><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>15</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mi>±</mi><msqrt><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msqrt></mrow></math>
(c) If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>
Hence solution : <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>

theory_sections.topics: Method II : Solution of a Quadratic Equation by Completing the Square
theory_sections.markdown:
## Method II : Solution of a Quadratic Equation by Completing the Square
Consider the quadratic equation, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>
(i) Shift constant term ' <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow></math> ' to the R.H.S. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></math>
(ii) Divide both sides of the quadratic equation by ' <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></math> '. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>⇒</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>
(iii) Write coefficient <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>⇒</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>
(iv) Add <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> on both sides of equal sign (=) and completing the whole square on L.H.S.
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>⇒</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>⇒</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>⇒</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>
(v) Taking square root on both sides of equal sign (=). <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>⇒</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>±</mi><mfrac><mrow><msqrt><mrow><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>
(vi) Now, shift <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> from L.H.S to R.H.S to get the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>.</mo><mo>⇒</mo><mspace width="1em" /><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mi>±</mi><mfrac><mrow><msqrt><mrow><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>⇒</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>±</mi><msqrt><mrow><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>
Solve the equation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>16</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>4</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> by completing the square.

theory_sections.topics: Method III : Solution of a Quadratic Equation by Using the Quadratic Formula
theory_sections.markdown:
## Method III : Solution of a Quadratic Equation by Using the Quadratic Formula
In the method II we see that solutions/roots of the quadratic equation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> by completing the square,
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>±</mi><msqrt><mrow><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>
We can use this equation (i) as a formula to find the solutions or roots of the quadratic equation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>.

## ILLUSTRATIOM : 5
Find the roots of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi></mrow><mrow><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">2</mn></mrow></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">3</mn></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">1</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">0</mn></mrow></mrow></math> by using the formula.

## NATURE OF ROOTS
For the quadratic equation: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> is called discriminant of the quadratic equation. The value of ( <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></math> ) is denoted by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>D</mi></mrow></math>.
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∴</mo><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></math>
The discriminant plays an important role in finding the nature of the roots of the quadratic equation.
(i) If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, then roots are real and equal.
(ii) If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, then roots are real and unequal.
(iii) If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, then roots are not real.

## ILLUSTRATIOM : 6
Find the nature of the roots of the following quadratic equations. If the real roots exist, find them:
(i) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>
(ii) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><msqrt><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msqrt><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>
(iii) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>

## SUM AND PRODUCT OF ROOTS
If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>α</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>β</mi></mrow></math> are the roots of quadratic equation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>D</mi></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>−</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>D</mi></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>, then
(i) Sum of roots, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>D</mi></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>−</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>D</mi></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>D</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>−</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>D</mi></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mtext> Coefficient of </mtext><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mtext> Coefficient of </mtext><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>
(ii) Product of roots, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>α</mi><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>D</mi></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>×</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>−</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>D</mi></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>D</mi></mrow></msqrt><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mtext> Constant term </mtext></mrow><mrow><mtext> Coefficient of </mtext><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>
For example in equation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>. Sum of roots <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math>, Product of roots <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math>

## Learn More
Condition for one root common: Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>α</mi></mrow></math> be the common root of the two equations, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>
Then, the condition for one root common is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>
Condition for both roots are common, is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>

## RELATION BETWEEN ROOTS AND COEFFICIENTS
If roots of quadratic equation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>α</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>β</mi></mrow></math>, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>·</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>
Now,
(i) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mspace width="1em" /><mi>α</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>β</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>α</mi><mi>β</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mfrac><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msqrt><mrow><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mi>D</mi></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>
(ii) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>α</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>α</mi><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mfrac><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>
(iii) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>α</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msqrt><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>β</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msqrt><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>α</mi><mi>β</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><msqrt><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mfrac><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi><msqrt><mrow><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi><msqrt><mrow><mi>D</mi></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>
(iv) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>α</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>α</mi><mi>β</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>α</mi><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>
(v) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>α</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>β</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>β</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>α</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>α</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><mi>α</mi><mi>β</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>α</mi><mi>β</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>α</mi><mi>β</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mfrac><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>
(vi) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>α</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi>β</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>α</mi><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>·</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>

## FORMATION OF A QUADRATIC EQUATION WHOSE ROOTS ARE GIVEN
If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>α</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>β</mi></mrow></math> are the roots of a quadratic equation, then the quadratic equadratic equation is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>α</mi><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> i.e. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo></mrow></math> sum of the roots <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo></mrow></math> product of the roots <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>

## GRAPH OF QUADRATIC EXPRESSIONS
Consider the expression <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow></math> then the graph between <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></math> is always a parabola. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, then the shape of the parabola is concave upward and if <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, then the shape of the parabola is concave downwards. There is only 6 possible graph of a quadratic expression as given below:
Case -I When <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">a</mi></mrow><mo>></mo><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">0</mn></mrow></mrow></math>
(i) If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>
(ii) If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>
(iii) If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">D</mi></mrow><mo><</mo><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">0</mn></mrow></mrow></math>
Case -II When <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">a</mi></mrow><mo><</mo><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">0</mn></mrow></mrow></math>
(i) If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>
(ii) If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">D</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">0</mn></mrow></mrow></math>
(iii) If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">D</mi></mrow><mo><</mo><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">0</mn></mrow></mrow></math>

## Learn More
Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></math> be real numbers and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, then the quadratic polynomial <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></math>, obtained the maximum value at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>
In this case, the graph of the quadratic polynomial is as given figure,
If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></math> be real numbers and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, then the quadratic polynomial <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></math>,
