## CASE-1 : Time to fill the tank
Illustration: Two pipes running together can fill a cistern in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>3</mn><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>13</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> minutes. If one pipe takes 3 minutes more than the other to fill it, find the time in which each pipe would fill the cistern.
Sol. Let the faster pipe takes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> minutes to fill the cistern. Therefore, the slower pipe will take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> minutes to fill the cistern.
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∴</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>40</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>13</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>40</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>13</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mn>13</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>41</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>120</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>13</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>24</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> or <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>24</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>13</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>⇒</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mspace width="1em" /><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mo>∵</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></math>

theory_sections.topics: CASE-2 : Time to fill the tank when both inlet and outlet working simultaneously.
theory_sections.markdown:
## CASE-2 : Time to fill the tank when both inlet and outlet working simultaneously.
Hence, the faster pipe fills the cistern in 5 minutes and the slower pipe takes 8 minutes to fill the cistern.
Illustration: If an outlet tap takes 1 hour more to empty the tank than an inlet tap to fill the tank. When both the taps opened together, then tank can be filled in 12 hours. Find the time to fill the tank by the inlet tap alone.
Sol. Let the inlet tap takes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> hours to fill the tank.
Therefore, the outlet tap will take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> hour to empty the tank.
∵ It is given that tank can be filled in 12 hours when both inlet and outlet tap works simultaneously. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∴</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>12</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>⇒</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mo>∵</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></math>
Hence, the water tank can be filled by inlet tap alone in 3 hours.
 tank in 7 hours. How many hours z alone fill the tank?
[Hint. Work done by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>z</mi></mrow></math> in 1 hour <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> 's in 1 hour <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> 's in 1 hour. Ans. 14 hours]
Sol. Suppose <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> be the number of hours required by the second pipe alone and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>V</mi></mrow></math> be the volume of the pool. Then, first pipe takes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> hours while the third pipe takes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> hours to fill the pool.
CASE-3 : Time to fill the swimming pool by three inlet pipes when opened for different time interval. Illustration: A swimming pool is filled with three pipes with uniform flow. The first two pipes operating simultaneously, fill the pool in the same time during which the pool is filled by the third pipe alone. The second pipe fills the pool five hours faster than the first pipe and four hours slower than the third pipe. Find the time required by each pipe to fill the pool separately.
Swimming Pool
Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></math> hours be the time taken by first and second pipe to fill the pool simultaneously, then the third pipe also takes the same time to fill the pool.
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>V</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>V</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>V</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>⇒</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>10</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>⇒</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mo>⇒</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mo>∵</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></math>
Hence, the time required to fill the tank by first pipe is 15 hrs , by second pipe is 10 hrs and by third pipe is 6 hrs .
Q 1. Three pipes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>z</mi></mrow></math> running together can fill a tank in 6 hours. All three pipes start together, after 2 hours third pipe <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>z</mi></mrow></math> was closed and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> and y filled the remaining
Q 2. A pipe can fill the tank is 4 hours. Due to leakage at the bottom it is filled in 5 hours. When the tank is full, in how much time will it be empties by the leak?
[Hint. Part empties in 1 hour <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>5</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> Ans. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow></math> hours]

## MISCELLANEOUS SOLVED EXAMPLES
1. Find the values of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow></math> for which the following equation has equal roots : <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>
Sol. We have, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>. Here, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∴</mo><mspace width="1em" /><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>×</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo><mo>⇒</mo><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>14</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>
The given equation will have equal roots, if <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>14</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> or, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>14</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow></math> or, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>14</mn></mrow></math>
2. Evaluate : <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>20</mn><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>20</mn><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>20</mn><mi>…</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>
Sol. Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>20</mn><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>20</mn><mi>…</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> or <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>. Therefore, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>20</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>
This gives <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>20</mn><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>404</mn></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>101</mn></mrow></msqrt></mrow></math> or <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>20</mn><mo>−</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>404</mn></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>−</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>101</mn></mrow></msqrt></mrow></math>
Since, the given expression can not be negative therefore, we neglect the negative value <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>−</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>101</mn></mrow></msqrt></mrow></math>. Hence, the desired value of the expression is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>101</mn></mrow></msqrt></mrow></math>.
3. Find the condition that the quadratic equations <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">a</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">b</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">0</mn></mrow></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">b</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">a</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">0</mn></mrow></mrow></math> may have a common root.
Sol. Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>α</mi></mrow></math> be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></math> common root of the given equations. Then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>α</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>α</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>
By the method of cross-multiplication, we get <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>α</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>α</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>. This gives <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>α</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>⇒</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>⇒</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> is the required condition.
4. Given that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></math> are the roots of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, find the equation with roots <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>β</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.
Sol. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>l</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>α</mi><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>l</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>m</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>l</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>. We know <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>β</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>α</mi><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>m</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>l</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mfrac><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>l</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>m</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>n</mi><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>l</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>

## SEQUENCE
The number patterns or arrangement of numbers according to definite rule or a set of rules is called a SEQUENCE.
The various numbers occuring in a sequence are called its terms. The <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term of the sequence is denoted by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math>. The <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term is also called the GENERAL TERM of the sequence. For example,
(i) The numbers <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>⟨</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi></mrow></math>.<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>⟩</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>q</mi><mi>u</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>w</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>h</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>u</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>𝐍</mi></mrow></math>.
(ii) The numbers <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">⟨</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow></math> represent a sequence written according to the rule <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>𝐍</mi></mrow></math>.
(iii) The numbers <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>⟨</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi></mrow></math>.<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>⟩</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>q</mi><mi>u</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>w</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>h</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>u</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>𝐍</mi></mrow></math>.
(iv) The numbers <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>⟨</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>13</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>21</mn><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>⟩</mi></mrow></math> represent a sequence written according to the rule <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>𝐍</mi></mrow></math>.
(v) The numbers <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>⟨</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi></mrow></math>.<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>⟩</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>q</mi><mi>u</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>w</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>h</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>f</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>f</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>u</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>s</mi><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>></mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>𝐍</mi></mrow></math>. This sequence of numbers is called the Fibonacci sequence.
(vi) The numbers <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>⟨</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>13</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo></mrow></math>. represent a sequence of prime numbers.
Note that in every sequence it is not always possible to write a specific formula.

## METHODS OF DESCRIBING A SEQUENCE
(i) A sequence may be described by writing first few terms till the rule for writing down the other terms is evident.
(ii) A sequence may be described by giving a formula for its general term (the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term).
(iii) A sequence may be described by specifying first few terms and a formula (or a set of formulae) giving a relation between successive terms. Such a formula is called RECURSIVE FORMULA (or RECURRENCE RELATION).
(iv) Some sequences may not be described by any rule.

## SERIES
If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">⟨</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow></math> is a sequence, then the expression <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>…</mi></mrow></math>. is called the series associated with the given sequence.

## PROGRESSION
A sequence is said to be a PROGRESSION if its terms numerically increase or numerically decrease continuously.

topics.summary:
## ARITHMETIC PROGRESSION (A.P.)
The sequence <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">⟨</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow></math> is called an arithmetic progression (A.P.), if the difference of the term and the preceding term is always same or constant i.e. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo></mrow></math> <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi></mrow></math>
In general, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo></mrow></math> Constant (denoted by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>d</mi></mrow></math> ), here <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> is a natural number.
The constant difference d is called the common difference of the A.P. First term <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> of the A.P. is denoted by ' <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></math> '. Hence the standard form of A.P. is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo></mrow></math>. The prominant Indian mathematician - astronomer Aryabhata gave the method of sum of finite arithmetic progression in 499 AD.
## Learn
If the sequence <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">⟨</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow></math> is an A.P., then
(i) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">⟨</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow></math> is an A.P., where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow></math> is a constant.
(ii) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">⟨</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow></math> is an A.P., where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow></math> is a constant.
(iii) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">⟨</mo><mi>k</mi><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mi>k</mi><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow></math> is an A.P., where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow></math> is a non-zero constant.
(iv) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">⟨</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>k</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>k</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>k</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow></math> is an A.P., where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow></math> is a non-zero constant.
## FORMULA FOR GENERAL TERM OF AN A.P.
The <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term of the A.P., is given by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></math>. Here <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> is the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term of the A.P.
## Learn More

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">{</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">}</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mo>∵</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>

If the sum of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> terms of an A.P. is given by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>, find its <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term.

It is given that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>∴</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo></mrow></math> (Sum of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> terms) - [Sum of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> terms] <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>⇒</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>
## ARITHMETIC MEAN(S) BETWEEN TWO NUMBERS
Arithmetic mean(s) between two numbers is/are the number(s) which when inserted between the two numbers, then the sequence obtained will be an Arithmetic Progression.
If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow></math> be an arithmetic mean between two numbers <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow></math>, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></math> will form an A.P. ∴ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>⇒</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>

Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> arithmetic means between two terms <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow></math>, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></math> will be in A.P.

Thus the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></math>-arithmetic means between <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow></math> are as follows:
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mi>;</mi><mspace width="1em" /><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mi>;</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>;</mi><mspace width="1em" /><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>

## GEOMETRIC PROGRESSION
The sequence <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi></mrow></math>. ; is called a geometric progression (G.P.) if <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi></mrow></math>, where none of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi></mrow></math> is zero. In general <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo></mrow></math> constant (say, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow></math> ), <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>𝐍</mi></mrow></math>.
The constant ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow></math> is called the common ratio of the G.P. If the first term <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> of the G.P. be taken as a , then the standard form of G.P. is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>r</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo></mrow></math>.
Formula for General Term of a G.P. : The <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term of the G.P. written in standard form is given by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>𝐍</mi></mrow></math>
Formula for Sum of First <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">n</mi></mrow></mrow></math> Terms of a G.P. : The sum of first <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> terms of the G.P., <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>, if <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>></mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>, if <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo><</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>
Note : (i) When <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>…</mi></mrow></math> upto <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> terms <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi><mi>a</mi></mrow></math>. (ii) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mspace width="1em" /><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>, etc.

If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo><</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>, the sum of infinite terms (S) of the G.P., <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>. Where ' <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></math> ' is the first term and ' <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow></math> ' is the common ratio of G.P. Consideration of terms of a G.P.
(i) If three terms to be selected in G.P., choose them as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow></math>.
(ii) If four terms to be selected in G.P. choose them as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>r</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.
Note that three numbers <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></math> are in G.P. if and only if <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> or if and only if <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>.</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></math>
Geometric Mean (G. M.) of Two Terms a and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">b</mi></mrow></mrow></math> : If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>G</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></math> are in G.P. ( <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow></math> are positive), then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>G</mi></mrow></math> is the GEOMETRIC MEAN of numbers <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow></math>. Which is given as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi></mrow></msqrt></mrow></math>
Inserting <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">n</mi></mrow></mrow></math> Geometric Means between Two Numbers <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">a</mi></mrow></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">b</mi></mrow></mrow></math> : Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow></math> be positive numbers and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>G</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>G</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>G</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> be such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>G</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>G</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>G</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></math> is a G.P. Then, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>⇒</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></msup></mrow></math>. Thus the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> geometric means between <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow></math> are :
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>G</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></msup><mi>;</mi><msub><mi>G</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></msup><mi>;</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>G</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></msup></mrow></math>
## RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN A.M. AND G.M.
Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>G</mi></mrow></math> be A.M. and G.M. of two given positive real numbers <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow></math> respectively, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi></mrow></msqrt></mrow></math> Thus, we have <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>−</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mrow><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo>−</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow></msqrt><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>G</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> Hence, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>≥</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow></math>.

Sum of first 8 terms <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><munder><munder><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⏟</mo></munder><mrow><mtext>cancelled out </mtext></mrow></munder><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow></math>
Thus, sum of first 3 terms = sum of first 8 terms
Now, sum of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>11</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> terms
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>
- In an A.P., if <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>p</mi><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>q</mi><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></math>, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo><</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>.
Consider an A.P.:
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mn>4</mn><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></math> and 7th term <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mn>9</mn><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></math>
Here <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></math> through illustrative examples.
[Here <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></math> ]
Let us understand the above concepts is a better way in different cases
CASE-I : Sum of terms equidistant from the beginning and end.
Illustration: Consider an A.P.: 2, 6, ....., 46; with 12 terms.
Find the sum of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mn>4</mn><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mn>9</mn><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> terms.
Sol. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>4</mn><msup><mrow /><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term from beginning <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term from end
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>⇒</mo><mspace width="1em" /><msup><mn>4</mn><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term from beginning <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>9</mn><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term from end.
Hence, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>4</mn><msup><mrow /><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>9</mn><msup><mrow /><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> terms are equidistant from beginning and end respectively of the A.P.
∴ Sum of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mn>4</mn><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mn>9</mn><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo></mrow></math> First term + Last term
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>46</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>48</mn></mrow></math>
CASE-II : Sum of first <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> terms equal to sum of first q terms
Illustration: Consider an A.P.: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi></mrow></math>. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>14</mn></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>14</mn></mrow></math>; then find the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mn>9</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>.
Sol. Since <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>14</mn><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>
i.e. sum of first 2 terms is equal to sum of first 7 terms.
Hence, sum of first ( <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></math> ) term <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>
CASE-III : <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>p</mi><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>q</mi><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></math>.
Illustration: If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term of an A.P. is equal to 18 and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mn>18</mn><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term of the same A.P. is equal to 10 , then find <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mn>15</mn><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term of the same A.P.
Sol. Since <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>18</mn></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mn>18</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∴</mo><mspace width="1em" /><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mn>15</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>18</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>13</mn></mrow></math>

Q. 1. The sum of the first five terms of an A.P. and the sum of the first seven terms of the same A.P. is 167 . If the sum of first 10 terms of this A.P. is 235 , find the sum of first twenty terms.
[Hint: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>167</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>235</mn><mspace width="1em" /></mrow></math> Ans. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mn>20</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>970</mn></mrow></math> ]

Ans. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mn>30</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2550</mn></mrow></math> ]

If 7 time the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mn>7</mn><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term of an A.P. is equal to the 12 times the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mn>12</mn><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term, then find the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>19</mn><msup><mrow /><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term

## MISCELLANEOUS SOLVED EXAMPLES
1. If the first term and common difference in an A.P. are 8 and -1 respectively, then find:
(i) general term
(ii) the progression
(iii) the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term and
(iv) the expression for sum to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">n</mi></mrow></mrow></math> terms and hence sum to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">1</mn><mn mathvariant="bold">0</mn></mrow></mrow></math> terms.
Sol. Given, the first term <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></math> and the common difference <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>
(i) The <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term of an A.P. is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></math>
Substituting <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>d</mi></mrow></math> in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>⇒</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>⇒</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></math>
(ii) By substituting <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi></mrow></math> in the general term <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></math>, we can generate the arithmetic progression <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>⇒</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mspace width="1em" /><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>⇒</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>⇒</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mspace width="1em" /><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>⇒</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math>
Hence the progression is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi></mrow></math>.
(iii) The <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term of the A.P. can be calculated by substituting <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></math> in the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> term <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>⇒</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>
(iv) The sum to ' <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ' terms of an A.P. is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></math>. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>⇒</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>⇒</mo><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo><mo>⇒</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>⇒</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mn>12</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></msub><mo>∴</mo><mn>6</mn><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mn>12</mn></mrow></msub><mo>⇒</mo><mn>6</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">[</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">[</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>12</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">]</mo></mrow><mo>⇒</mo><mn>18</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>200</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>30</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>200</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>11</mn><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>⇒</mo><mn>3600</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>90</mn><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6000</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>330</mn><mi>d</mi><mo>⇒</mo><mn>90</mn><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>330</mn><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6000</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3600</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>240</mn><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2400</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2400</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>240</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></math>

Hence, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>78</mn></mrow></math>.
