Sol. Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> be the required point and the given points be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>13</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>.
Then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>P</mi><mi>B</mi></mrow></math> (given)
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>⇒</mo><msqrt><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>0</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>13</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>0</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></msqrt><mo>⇒</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>144</mn><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>169</mn><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></msqrt></mrow></math>
Taking square on both sides, we get
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>144</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>169</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>⇒</mo><mn>10</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>
∴ The required point on <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>Y</mi></mrow></math>-axis is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>.
4. Find the ratio in which the join of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> is divided by (i) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>𝐗</mi></mrow></math>-axis (ii) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>𝐘</mi></mrow></math>-axis.
Sol. (i) X -axis divides the join of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> in the ratio of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mi>:</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>:</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>:</mi><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>.
(ii) Y -axis divides, in the ratio of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mi>:</mi><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>:</mi><mn>5</mn></mrow></math>.
5. Find the co-ordinates of a point which divides the line segment joining the points <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> in the ratio 1:4 internally.
Sol. Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> be the given points and let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> divide <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi></mrow></math> in the ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mi>:</mi><mn>4</mn></mrow></math> internally.
Using section formula, we have
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>×</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfrac><mtext> and </mtext><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>×</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>13</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∴</mo><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>13</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> divides AB in the ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mi>:</mi><mn>4</mn></mrow></math> internally.
6. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi></mrow></math> is a triangle in which <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow></math> are the mid-points of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi></mrow></math> respectively. The coordinates are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. Find <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mover><mrow><mi>R</mi><mi>Q</mi></mrow><mo accent="true">―</mo></mover></mrow></math>.
Sol. Let the coordinates of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi></mrow></math> be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>.
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>⇒</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>⇒</mo><mspace width="1em" /><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></math>
Let the coordinates of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi></mrow></math> be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>.
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>⇒</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>⇒</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></math>
Coordinates of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mover><mrow><mi>R</mi><mi>Q</mi></mrow><mo accent="true">―</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>73</mn></mrow></msqrt></mrow></math>
7. The coordinates of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi></mrow></math> are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>,</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> respectively. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>E</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>F</mi></mrow></math> are the mid-points of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi><mi>A</mi></mrow></math> and AB respectively. Calculate the area of the triangle DEF .
Sol. Mid-point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>D</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>
Mid-point E <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>
Mid-point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>F</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>
Now, using the formula, area of triangle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">|</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">|</mo></mrow></mrow></math>
⇒ Area of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mi>D</mi><mi>E</mi><mi>F</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></math> square units.
Hence, the area of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mi>D</mi><mi>E</mi><mi>F</mi></mrow></math> is 4 square units.
8. What kind of triangle is formed by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> ?
Sol. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow></math>

Here, the points are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>.

Here, the points are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>11</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>

For given three points <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></math> to decide whether they are collinear or vertices of a particular triangle. First we find the length of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mi>A</mi></mrow></math> then we shall find that the point are
Collinear, if the sum of two shorter distances is equal to the longest distance

Vertices of an equilateral triangle if <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>C</mi><mi>A</mi></mrow></math>

Vertices of an isosceles triangle if <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi></mrow></math> or <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>C</mi><mi>A</mi></mrow></math> or <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi></mrow></math>

Vertices of a right angled triangle if <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>B</mi><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>C</mi><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> or <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> or <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>A</mi><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>B</mi><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math>

For given four points <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>D</mi></mrow></math>;

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>D</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>;</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>D</mi><mo>⇒</mo><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi></mrow></math> is a square.

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>D</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>;</mi><mo>⇒</mo><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi></mrow></math> is a rhombus.

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>D</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>;</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>D</mi><mo>⇒</mo><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi></mrow></math> is a rectangle.

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>D</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>;</mi><mo>⇒</mo><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi></mrow></math> is a parallelogram.
(a) Diagonal of square, rhombus, rectangle and parallelogram always bisect each other
Diagonal of rhombus and square bisect each other at right angle.
Three given points are collinear if area of the triangle formed from these three points is zero.

theory_sections.topics: PLOTTING OF A POINT WHOSE COORDINATES ARE KNOWN
theory_sections.markdown:
## PLOTTING OF A POINT WHOSE COORDINATES ARE KNOWN
The point can be plotted by measuring its proper distances from both the axes. Thus, any point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> can be plotted as follows :
(i) Measure <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>O</mi><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> equal to h along the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>X</mi></mrow></math>-axis.
(ii) Now measure <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> perpendicular to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>O</mi><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow></math>.
The method of describing the location of points in a plane was proposed by the great French mathematician Rene' Descartes in 17th century. Rene' Descartes' Latinized name is Renatius Cartesius and from here the terminology "Cartisian plane" and "Cartisian coordinate system" are derived.

## DISTANCE BETWEEN TWO POINTS
Distance between any two points <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> in the plane is the length of the line segment <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>Q</mi></mrow></math>.
From <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>Q</mi></mrow></math> draw perpendiculars <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>L</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> respectively on the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>X</mi></mrow></math>-axis and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>R</mi></mrow></math> perpendicular on <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mi>M</mi></mrow></math>.
Then, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>O</mi><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>O</mi><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>P</mi><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∴</mo><mi>P</mi><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>L</mi><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>O</mi><mi>M</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>O</mi><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>Q</mi><mi>M</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>R</mi><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>Q</mi><mi>M</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>P</mi><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>
Since <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>Q</mi></mrow></math> is a right angled triangle,
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∴</mo><mspace width="1em" /><mi>P</mi><msup><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>P</mi><msup><mi>R</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>Q</mi><msup><mi>R</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math>
(By the Pythagoras Theorem)
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∴</mo><mi>P</mi><mi>Q</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></msqrt></mrow></math>
i.e., Distance between any two points <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mtext> difference of abscissae </mtext><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mtext> difference of ordinates </mtext><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></msqrt></mrow></math>
Corollary : The distance of the point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> from the origin <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msqrt><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><msubsup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow></msqrt></mrow></math>
Coordinate geometry is used to manage and regulate the location of air transport. Coordinate system is used in the Global Positioning System (GPS) which provides location and time information in all weather conditions. In a GPS, the longitude and the latitude of a place are its coordinates. The distance formula is used to find the distance between two places in a GPS.

## APPLICATIONS OF DISTANCE FORMULA
(i) For given three points <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></math> to decide whether they are collinear or vertices of a particular triangle. First we find the length of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mi>A</mi></mrow></math> then we shall find that the point are
(a) Collinear, if the sum of two shorter distances is equal to the longest distance
(b) Vertices of an equilateral triangle if <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>C</mi><mi>A</mi></mrow></math>
(c) Vertices of an isosceles triangle if <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi></mrow></math> or <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>C</mi><mi>A</mi></mrow></math> or <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi></mrow></math>
(d) Vertices of a right angled triangle if <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>B</mi><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>C</mi><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> or <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> or <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>A</mi><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>B</mi><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math>
(ii) For given four points <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>D</mi></mrow></math>;
(a) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>D</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>;</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>D</mi><mo>⇒</mo><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi></mrow></math> is a square.
(b) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>D</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>;</mi><mo>⇒</mo><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi></mrow></math> is a rhombus.
(c) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>D</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>;</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>D</mi><mo>⇒</mo><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi></mrow></math> is a rectangle.
(d) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>D</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>;</mi><mo>⇒</mo><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi></mrow></math> is a parallelogram.
(iii) (a) Diagonal of square, rhombus, rectangle and parallelogram always bisect each other
(b) Diagonal of rhombus and square bisect each other at right angle.
(c) Three given points are collinear if area of the triangle formed from these three points is zero.
(d) Four given points are collinear, if area of quadrilateral formed from these four points is zero.

## SECTION FORMULA
To find the co-ordinates of a point, which divides a line segment joining two points internally in a given ratio :
Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> be the two given points and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> be a point on <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi></mrow></math>, which divides it internally in the given ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>:</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> i.e., <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>:</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>:</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math>.
We have to find the co-ordinates of P . Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>.
Draw the perpendiculars <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>L</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>P</mi><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> and B respectively on <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math>-axis and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>K</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>P</mi><mi>T</mi></mrow></math> from A and P on <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> respectively. Now, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mspace width="1em" /><mi>A</mi><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>L</mi><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>O</mi><mi>M</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>O</mi><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>&</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>M</mi><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>O</mi><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>O</mi><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mspace linebreak="newline" /><mi>&</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>M</mi><mi>P</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>M</mi><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>M</mi><mi>P</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>L</mi><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mspace linebreak="newline" /><mi>&</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>N</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>N</mi><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>N</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>M</mi><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></mrow></math>
From (i), we have, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>
Now, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>⇒</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>m</mi><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∴</mo><mspace width="1em" /><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>m</mi><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>
Now, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="1em" /><mo>⇒</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>m</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>
Hence, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mspace width="1em" /><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>m</mi><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>m</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>
Therefore, co-ordinates of a point which divides the line segment joining the points <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> in the ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>:</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> internally is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>m</mi><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>m</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>
The coordinates of a point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi></mrow></math> which divides line segment joining two points <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi></mrow></math> externally in the ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>:</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>m</mi><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>n</mi><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>·</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>m</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>n</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>

## MID-POINT FORMULA
The co-ordinates of the mid-point of the line segment joining two points <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> can be obtained by taking <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> in the section formula given above. Putting <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> in the section formula, we have
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>n</mi><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mtext> and </mtext><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>n</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>
Hence, co-ordinates of the mid-point joining two points <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>
Prove that the points <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>𝐀</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">5</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐁</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>𝐂</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">5</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> are the vertices of an isosceles right-angled triangle. Find the coordinates of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>D</mi></mrow></math> so that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi></mrow></math> is a square.

## POINTS OF TRISECTION
Trisection means a line is dividing into three equal parts.
This can be done by finding two points <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>D</mi></mrow></math> on the line segment <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi></mrow></math>, such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>D</mi><mi>B</mi></mrow></math>
Let us assume <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>D</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></math>
Then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>D</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>p</mi></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∴</mo><mspace width="1em" /><mi>A</mi><mi>C</mi><mi>:</mi><mi>C</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi><mi>:</mi><mn>2</mn><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>:</mi><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>
Also, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>D</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∴</mo><mspace width="1em" /><mi>A</mi><mi>D</mi><mi>:</mi><mi>D</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>p</mi><mi>:</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>:</mi><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>
Hence, we can conclude that, to find points of trisection, we find two points <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>D</mi></mrow></math> which divides AB in the ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mi>:</mi><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>:</mi><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>, respectively.

## CONNECTING TOPIC

## 1. Centroid of a Triangle
The centroid G is the point of intersection of medians <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi></mrow></mrow></math> and CF , which are the lines joining a vertex with the mid-point of opposite side.
The coordinates of the centroid G are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>.
where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>

## 2. Incentre of the Triangle
The incentre I is the centre of circle touching the sides of the triangle internally, called INCIRCLE and it is the point of intersection of the internal bisectors. AP, BQ, CR of the vertex angles.
The coordinates of incentre I are given by
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>,
where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow></mrow></math> are the sides of the triangle.
3. Circumcentre of the Triangle
The circumcentre <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>O</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> is the centre of the circle passing through the vertices of triangle and it is the point of intersection of perpendicular bisectors of the sides of triangle.
Thus, we have <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>O</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>O</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>O</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><mi>C</mi></mrow></math>
Circumcentre of a right angled triangle is the mid points of its hypotenuse.
4. Orthocentre: It is the point of intersection of perpendicular drawn from vertices on opposite sides of a triangle.
Remarks: (i) If the triangle is equilateral, the centroid, incentre, orthocentre, circumcentre coincides.
(ii) Orthocentre, centroid and cirumcentre are always collinear.
(iii) In an isosceles triangle, centroid, orthocentre, incentre, circumcentre lies on the same line.

## AREA OF A TRIANGLE
Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi></mrow></math> be any triangle whose vertices are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>. Draw <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mi>L</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>A</mi><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> perpendiculars from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi></mrow></math> respectively on the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>X</mi></mrow></math>-axis. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>A</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>N</mi><mi>C</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>N</mi><mi>C</mi></mrow></math> are all trapeziums.
Area of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo></mrow></math> Area of trapezium <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>M</mi><mo>+</mo></mrow></math> Area of trapezium <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>N</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>−</mo></mrow></math> Area of trapezium <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>N</mi><mi>C</mi></mrow></math>
We know that, Area of trapezium
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>×</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mtext> Sum of parallel sides </mtext><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>×</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mtext> Distance between the paralleled sides </mtext><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>
Therefore, area of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>L</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>A</mi><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>L</mi><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mi>M</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>L</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>L</mi><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>&</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mspace linebreak="newline" /><mi>&</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">[</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math>
Since area of a triangle is always positive, therefore we reject the negative sign if appear in the value of area of the triangle.
Note: (i) Area of triangle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>×</mo></mrow></math> Base × Altitude
(ii) Area of polygon can be calculated by dividing it into the triangular region.
(iii) If area of triangle formed by joining three points is zero, then points are collinear.

## AREA OF A QUADRILATERAL
Let the vertices of quadrilateral <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi></mrow></math> be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>D</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>
So, area of quadrilateral <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo></mrow></math> Area of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>+</mo></mrow></math> Area of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi></mrow></math>

## Learn More
Area of a quadrilateral with vertices <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> is given by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">|</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true"
