From figure, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>Q</mi><mi>S</mi><mi>R</mi></mrow></math> is a square.
Since, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>R</mi><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>Q</mi><mi>S</mi></mrow></math>, therefore <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>R</mi><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>Q</mi><mi>S</mi></mrow></math>
Since, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, therefore <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>
So, radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>

## 11. Constructions
## DIVISION OF A LINE SEGMENT
In this concept, we will learn the method of dividing a line segment internally in a given ratio.
You can easily understand this concept through the following illustration.
## SOLUTION :
Steps of construction :
(i) Draw a line segment AB of length 12 cm by using a ruler.
(ii) Draw a ray AX making a suitable acute angle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></mrow></mrow></math> with AB .
(iii) Along AX , draw <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> arcs intersecting the ray AX at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>
(iv) Join B to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>.
(v) Through <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> draw a line <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> parallel to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow></mrow></math> by making <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> equal
to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, which intersects AB at point P .
The point P so obtained is the required point, which divides AB internally in the ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>:</mi><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>.
## Alternative Method for Division of a Line Segment Internally in a Given Ratio
Use the following steps to divide a given line segment AB internally in a given ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>:</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> are natural numbers.
## Steps of construction :
(i) Draw a line segment AB of given length.
(ii) Draw a ray AX making a suitable acute angle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></mrow></mrow></math> with AB .
(iii) Draw a ray <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mi>Y</mi></mrow></math>, on opposite side of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>X</mi></mrow></math> with respect to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi></mrow></math>, parallel to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>X</mi></mrow></math> by making an angle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Y</mi></mrow></mrow></math> equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
(iv) Draw arcs intersecting the ray AX at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, and ray BY at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> such that
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>B</mi><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math>
(v) Join <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math>. Suppose it intersects AB at P .
The point P is the required point, which divide AB in the ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>:</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> internally.
## SOLUTION :
Steps of construction :
(i) Draw a line segment AB of length 6 cm .
(ii) Draw a ray AX making a suitable acute angle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></mrow></mrow></math> with AB .

Case (a): To draw the tangent to a circle at a given point on it, when the centre of the circle is known :
Required : To draw the tangent to the circle at P .
Steps of construction :
(i) Take a point O as centre and draw a circle of given radius.
(ii) Take a point P on the circle.
(iii) Join OP.
(iv) Draw a line AB perpendicular to OP at the point P . Line APB is the required tangent at P .
Circle can have at most 2 parallel tangents, one at a point on it and the other at a point diametrically ?
opposite to it.

## CONSTRUCTION OF TANGENTS TO A CIRCLE FROM A POINT OUTSIDE THE CIRCLE
In this situation, when the point lies outside the circle, there will be two tangents to the circle from this point.
In this construction, again we have two different situations:
Case (a) : To draw the tangents to a circle from a point outside it (external point), when its centre is known.
Given : A circle with centre O and a point P outside it.
Required : To construct the tangents to the circle from point P .
Steps of construction :
(i) Join OP and bisect it. Let M be the mid-point of OP .
(ii) Taking M as centre and MO as radius, draw a circle which intersect the given circle in two points, say A and B .
(iii) Join P to A and P to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>.</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow></mrow></math> and PB are the required tangents from P to given circle .

Given : A point P is at a distance of 6 cm . from the centre of a circle with radius 2.5 cm .
Required : To draw two tangents to the circle from the given point P .
Steps of construction :
(i) Draw a line segment OP of length 6 cm .
(ii) With centre O and radius equal to 2.5 cm , draw a circle.
(iii) Draw the right bisector of OP , which intersects OP at M .
(iv) Taking M as centre and MO as radius, draw a circle, which intersect the given circle in two points, say A and B .
(v) Join PA and PB . These are the required tangents from P to the given circle.
Case (b): To draw the tangents to a circle from a point outside it (external point), when its centre is not known.

Step 3: Bisect <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> at P and draw a circle taking P as centre and radius equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> or <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>.
Step 4: Draw another circle with radius equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3.5</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, taking the centre of larger circle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> intersecting the circle drawn in step 3 at A and B .
Step 5: Join <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow></mrow></math> and produce <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow></mrow></math> to meet the outer circle at S and T respectively.
Step 6: Draw line segments <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>U</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>V</mi></mrow></math>, such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>U</mi><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mi>S</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>V</mi><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mi>T</mi></mrow></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi></mrow></math> arc points on the circle with centre <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>.
Step 7: Join SU and TV. These are the required direct common tangents.
## Learn More
Locute the centre of a circular disk.
Hint: Perpendicular bisectors of two non parallel chords of circle passes through the centre of the circle.
## Steps of construction:
(i) Draw two non parallel chords of any length AB and PQ .
(ii) Draw perpendicular bisectors XY and LM of AB and PQ respectively, which intersect at point O .
So, O is the required centre of circle.
## MISCELLANEOUS SOLVED EXAMPLES
1. Draw a triangle ABC with side <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>45</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><mo>∠</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>75</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math>. Construct a triangle whose sides are (4/3) times the corresponding side of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
Sol. Steps of construction :
(i) Draw <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
(ii) Draw a ray BX and CY such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>45</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math> and
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Y</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>180</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msup><mn>45</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>75</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>60</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math>
Suppose BX and CY intersect at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>.</mo><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, so obtained is the given triangle.
(iii) Draw a ray BZ making an acute angle with BC on opposite side of vertex A with respect to BC .
(iv) Draw four (greater of 4 and 3 in 4/3) arcs intersecting the rays BZ at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>.
(v) Join <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> to C and draw a line through <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> parallel to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mi>C</mi></mrow></math>, intersecting the extended line segment BC at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.
(vi) Draw a line through <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> parallel to CA intersecting the extended line segment BA at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.
Triangle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> so obtained is the required triangle.
2. Construct a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math> in which <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>7.5</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>. Now construct a triangle similar to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math> such that each of its sides is third-fourth
of the corresponding sides of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math>. Also prove your assertion.
Sol. Steps of construction :
(i) Draw a line segment <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
(ii) With B as centre and radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, draw an arc.
(iii) With C as centre and radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>7.5</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, draw another arc, intersecting the arc drawn in step (ii) at the point A .
(iv) Join A to B and C to obtain <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
(v) Below BC draw ray BX , making an acute angle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
(vi) Draw four arcs intersecting the ray BX at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>
(vii) Join <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mi>C</mi></mrow></math>.
(viii) Since we have to construct a triangle each of whose sides is third-fourth of the corresponding sides of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math>. Hence draw <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mi>C</mi></mrow></math>.
(ix) From <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>, draw <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, intersecting BA at point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>. Then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> is the required triangle.
3. Construct a triangle similar to a given equilateral <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></mrow></mrow></math> with side 5 cm such that each
of its sides is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">6</mn></mrow></mrow><mrow><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">7</mn></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> th of the corresponding side of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
Sol. Steps of construction :
(i) Draw a line segment <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>
(ii) With Q as centre and radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, draw an arc.
(iii) With R as centre and radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, draw another arc intersecting the arc drawn in step (ii) at the point P .
(iv) Join PQ and PR to obtain <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
(v) Below QR , draw ray QX making an acute angle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
(vi) Draw seven arcs intersecting the ray QX at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>; such that
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>
(vii) Join <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></msub><mi>R</mi></mrow></math>.
(viii) Draw <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></msub><mi>R</mi></mrow></math>, intersecting QR at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>
(ix) From <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> draw <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, intersecting the QP at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.
We get required <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>Q</mi><msup><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> similar to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>Q</mi><mi>R</mi></mrow></math>.
4. Construct a triangle similar to a given triangle ABC with its sides equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">7</mn></mrow></mrow><mrow><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">5</mn></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> th of the corresponding sides of triangle ABC .
Sol. Steps of construction :

Steps of construction :
(i) Draw a circle of 3 cm radius with centre O .
(ii) Draw a circle of 5 cm radius, taking O as centre. Locate a point P on circle and join OP .
(iii) Bisect OP . Let M be midpoint of OP .
(iv) Taking M as its centre and MO as its radius, draw a circle. Let it intersect the smaller circle at points <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>Q</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>R</mi></mrow></math>.

## Justification:
Since PQ and PR are of lengths 4 cm each.
For <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi></mrow></mrow></math> is tangent at Q .
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mi>&</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>90</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mspace linebreak="newline" /><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mi>&</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mspace linebreak="newline" /><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mi>&</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></math>
By Pythagoras theorem in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow></mrow></math>,
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi>&</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mspace linebreak="newline" /><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi>&</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mspace linebreak="newline" /><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi>&</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>9</mn><mspace linebreak="newline" /><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi>&</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn><mspace linebreak="newline" /><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi></mrow><mi>&</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></math>
Thus justified.

## Steps of construction:

Given, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>45</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math>. Steps of construction :
(i) Draw a line <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.

To construct a triangle whose sides are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> of the corresponding sides of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
(v) Draw any ray AY making an acute angle with AC on the opposite to the vertex <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi></mrow></math>.
(vi) Locate 5 (the greater of 3 and 5 in 3/5) points <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> on AY so that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>.
(vii) Join <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub><mi>C</mi></mrow></math> and draw a line through <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> (the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>3</mn><msup><mrow /><mrow><mtext>rd </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> point, 3 being smaller of 3 and 5 in 3/5) parallel to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub><mi>C</mi></mrow></math> to intersect AC at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.
(viii) Draw a line through <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> parallel to the line CB to intersect AB at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.
Then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> is the required triangle.
For justification of the construction, note that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>Δ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mi>~</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∵</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><mi>C</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>
Therefore,
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow><mrow><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><mi>C</mi></mrow><mrow><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><mi>C</mi></mrow><mrow><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>,
i.e., <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>
Also, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> is parallel to CB .
Therefore, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>

## Steps of construction :
