Along AX , draw <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> arcs intersecting the ray AX at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>
Join B to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>.

Through <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> draw a line <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> parallel to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow></mrow></math> by making <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> equal
Draw a line segment AB of given length.

Draw a ray <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mi>Y</mi></mrow></math>, on opposite side of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>X</mi></mrow></math> with respect to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi></mrow></math>, parallel to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>X</mi></mrow></math> by making an angle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Y</mi></mrow></mrow></math> equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.

Draw arcs intersecting the ray AX at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, and ray BY at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> such that

Join <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math>. Suppose it intersects AB at P .
Draw a line segment AB of length 6 cm .

Draw a ray BY parallel to AX by making <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Y</mi></mrow></mrow></math> equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.

Draw three arcs intersecting the ray AX at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> and 4 arcs intersecting the ray BY at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> such that

Join <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>. Suppose it intersects AB at a point P .

Steps of construction when <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">m</mi></mrow><mo><</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">n</mi></mrow></mrow></math> :
Construct the given triangle ABC by using the given data.
Take any one of the three side of the given triangle as base. Let AB be the base of the given triangle ABC .
At one end, say A , of the base AB draw a ray AX below AB making a suitable acute angle with AB .

Along AX mark n points <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> such that
Join <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> to B .

Draw <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow></msub><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> parallel to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mi>B</mi></mrow></math> by making <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mi>A</mi><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow></msub><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mi>B</mi></mrow></math>, which meets AB at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.

theory_sections.markdown: ## 11. Constructions

## DIVISION OF A LINE SEGMENT
In this concept, we will learn the method of dividing a line segment internally in a given ratio.
You can easily understand this concept through the following illustration.

theory_sections.topics: Alternative Method for Division of a Line Segment Internally in a Given Ratio
theory_sections.markdown:
## Alternative Method for Division of a Line Segment Internally in a Given Ratio
Use the following steps to divide a given line segment AB internally in a given ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>:</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> are natural numbers.

## Steps of construction :
(i) Draw a line segment AB of given length.
(ii) Draw a ray AX making a suitable acute angle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></mrow></mrow></math> with AB .
(iii) Draw a ray <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mi>Y</mi></mrow></math>, on opposite side of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>X</mi></mrow></math> with respect to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi></mrow></math>, parallel to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>X</mi></mrow></math> by making an angle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Y</mi></mrow></mrow></math> equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
(iv) Draw arcs intersecting the ray AX at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, and ray BY at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> such that
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>B</mi><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math>
(v) Join <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math>. Suppose it intersects AB at P .
The point P is the required point, which divide AB in the ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>:</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> internally.

theory_sections.topics: CONSTRUCTION OF A TRIANGLE SIMILAR TO A GIVEN TRIANGLE (AS PER GIVEN SCALE FACTOR)
theory_sections.markdown: ## CONSTRUCTION OF A TRIANGLE SIMILAR TO A GIVEN TRIANGLE (AS PER GIVEN SCALE FACTOR)

## Scale Factor
The ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow></math> : <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> of the side of the triangle to be constructed and the corresponding side of the given triangle is known as their scale factor.
In this construction, there are two different situations:
(I) Steps of construction when <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">m</mi></mrow><mo><</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">n</mi></mrow></mrow></math> :
(i) Construct the given triangle ABC by using the given data.
(ii) Take any one of the three side of the given triangle as base. Let AB be the base of the given triangle ABC .
(iii) At one end, say A , of the base AB draw a ray AX below AB making a suitable acute angle with AB .
(iv) Along AX mark n points <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> such that
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>.</mo></mrow></math>
(v) Join <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> to B .
(vi) Draw <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow></msub><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> parallel to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mi>B</mi></mrow></math> by making <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mi>A</mi><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow></msub><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mi>B</mi></mrow></math>, which meets AB at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.
(vii) From <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>, draw <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> parallel to BC by making <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, which meets AC at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>. Triangle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> is the required triangle, each of whose sides is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mtext>th </mtext></mrow></msup></mrow></math> of the corresponding side of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.

## Steps of construction :
(i) Draw a line segment <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
(ii) With A as centre and radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, draw an arc above AB .
(iii) With B as centre and radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, draw another arc, intersecting the arc drawn in step (ii) at C.
(iv) Join A to C and B to C to obtain <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
(v) Below AB , draw a ray AX making a suitable acute angle with AB on opposite side of C with respect to AB .
(vi) Draw three arcs intersecting the ray AX at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>.
(vii) Join <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> to B .
(viii) Draw <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> parallel to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> by making <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, which meets AB at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.
(ix) From <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>, draw <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> parallel to BC by making <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, which meets AC at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>Δ</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> is the required triangle, each of the whose sides is two-third of the corresponding sides of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
(II) Steps of construction when <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">m</mi></mrow><mo>></mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">n</mi></mrow></mrow></math> :
(i) Construct the given triangle by using the given data.
(ii) Take any one of the three sides of the given triangle and consider it as the base. Let AB be the base of the given triangle ABC .
(iii) At one end, say A , of base AB draw a ray AX making a suitable acute angle with base AB on the opposite side of the vertex C with respect to AB .
(iv) Draw m arcs intersecting the ray AX at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math>.
(v) Join <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi></mrow></math>
(vi) Draw a line through <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> parallel to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mi>B</mi></mrow></math> by making <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow></msub><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mi>B</mi></mrow></math>, which intersects the extended line segment AB at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.
(vii) Draw a line through <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> parallel to BC by making <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, which intersects the extended line segment AC at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>
(viii) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>Δ</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> so obtained is the required triangle.

## Steps of construction :
(i) Draw <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
(ii) Draw a ray BX and CY such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>45</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math> and
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Y</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>180</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msup><mn>45</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>105</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>30</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math>
Suppose BX and CY intersect each other at A .
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math> so obtained is the given triangle.
(iii) Draw a ray BZ making a suitable acute angle with BC on opposite side of vertex A with respect to BC .
(iv) Draw four arcs intersecting the ray BZ at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>.
(v) Join <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> to C and draw a line through <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> parallel to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mi>C</mi></mrow></math> by making <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mi>C</mi></mrow></math>, which intersects the extended line segment BC at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.
(vi) Draw a line through <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> parallel to CA by making <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> equal to
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>30</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>, which intersects the extended line segment BA at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>. Triangle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> so obtained is the required triangle.

theory_sections.topics: To construct an equilateral triangle circumscribed over a circle of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">r</mi></mrow><mrow><mtext mathvariant="bold"> </mtext><mi mathvariant="bold">c</mi><mi mathvariant="bold">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
theory_sections.markdown: ## To construct an equilateral triangle circumscribed over a circle of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">r</mi></mrow><mrow><mtext mathvariant="bold"> </mtext><mi mathvariant="bold">c</mi><mi mathvariant="bold">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.

## Steps of Construction
Step 1: Draw a circle of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>r</mi><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math> with centre O .
Step 2: Draw radii OP, OQ and OR such that
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>120</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mo>∴</mo><mspace width="1em" /><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>120</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>
Step 3: At <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Q</mi></mrow></math> and R draw perpendiculars to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi></mrow></mrow></math> and OR respectively to from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>Δ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mo>.</mo><mi>Δ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math> is the required circumscribing equilateral triangle.

theory_sections.topics: CONSTRUCTION OF A TANGENT TO A CIRCLE (AT A GIVEN POINT)
theory_sections.markdown:
## CONSTRUCTION OF A TANGENT TO A CIRCLE (AT A GIVEN POINT)
Case (a): To draw the tangent to a circle at a given point on it, when the centre of the circle is known :
Required : To draw the tangent to the circle at P .
Steps of construction :
(i) Take a point O as centre and draw a circle of given radius.
(ii) Take a point P on the circle.
(iii) Join OP.
(iv) Draw a line AB perpendicular to OP at the point P . Line APB is the required tangent at P .
Circle can have at most 2 parallel tangents, one at a point on it and the other at a point diametrically ?
opposite to it.

theory_sections.topics: To draw the circum-circle of a given triangle.
theory_sections.markdown: ## To draw the circum-circle of a given triangle.

## Steps of Construction
Step 1: Draw <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math> with the given measurements.
Step 2: Draw perpendicular bisectors of the two of the sides, say AB and AC to intersect at O .
Step 3: Taking O as centre, and the radius equal to AO or BO or CO , draw a circle. The circle passes through all the vertices <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow></math> and C of the triangle. ∴ The circle drawn is the required circum-circle.

theory_sections.topics: CONSTRUCTION OF TANGENTS TO A CIRCLE FROM A POINT OUTSIDE THE CIRCLE
theory_sections.markdown:
## CONSTRUCTION OF TANGENTS TO A CIRCLE FROM A POINT OUTSIDE THE CIRCLE
In this situation, when the point lies outside the circle, there will be two tangents to the circle from this point.
In this construction, again we have two different situations:
Case (a) : To draw the tangents to a circle from a point outside it (external point), when its centre is known.
Given : A circle with centre O and a point P outside it.
Required : To construct the tangents to the circle from point P .
Steps of construction :
(i) Join OP and bisect it. Let M be the mid-point of OP .
(ii) Taking M as centre and MO as radius, draw a circle which intersect the given circle in two points, say A and B .
(iii) Join P to A and P to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>.</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow></mrow></math> and PB are the required tangents from P to given circle .

## Step of construction :
(i) Draw a circle of radius 4 cm .
(ii) Take a point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> outside the circle and draw a secant <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi></mrow></math>, which intersects the circle at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi></mrow></math>.
(iii) Produce <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi></mrow></math> such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>C</mi><mi>P</mi></mrow></math>.
(iv) Draw a semi-circle with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mi>B</mi></mrow></math> as diameter.
(v) Draw <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>D</mi><mi>⟂</mi><mi>C</mi><mi>B</mi></mrow></math>, which intersects the semi-circle at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>D</mi></mrow></math>.
(vi) With <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> as centre and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>D</mi></mrow></math> as radius draw arcs to intersect the given circle at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>T</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.
(vii) Join <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>T</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>. Then, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>T</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><msup><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> are the required tangents.
To construct the direct common tangents to the circles of radii 3.5 cm and 1.5 cm whose centres are 6.5 cm apart.
Step 1: Draw line segment, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>6.5</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
Step 2: Draw circles with radii 3.5 cm and 1.5 cm respectively with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> as centres.
Step 3: Bisect <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> at P and draw a circle taking P as centre and radius equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> or <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>.
Step 4: Draw another circle with radius equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3.5</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, taking the centre of larger circle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> intersecting the circle drawn in step 3 at A and B .
Step 5: Join <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow></mrow></math> and produce <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow></mrow></math> to meet the outer circle at S and T respectively.
Step 6: Draw line segments <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>U</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>V</mi></mrow></math>, such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>U</mi><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mi>S</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>V</mi><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mi>T</mi></mrow></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi></mrow></math> arc points on the circle with centre <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>.
Step 7: Join SU and TV. These are the required direct common tangents.

## Learn More
Locute the centre of a circular disk.
Hint: Perpendicular bisectors of two non parallel chords of circle passes through the centre of the circle.

## Steps of construction:
(i) Draw two non parallel chords of any length AB and PQ .
(ii) Draw perpendicular bisectors XY and LM of AB and PQ respectively, which intersect at point O .
So, O is the required centre of circle.

## MISCELLANEOUS SOLVED EXAMPLES
1. Draw a triangle ABC with side <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>45</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><mo>∠</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>75</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math>. Construct a triangle whose sides are (4/3) times the corresponding side of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
Sol. Steps of construction :
(i) Draw <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
(ii) Draw a ray BX and CY such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>45</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math> and
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Y</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>180</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msup><mn>45</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>75</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>60</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math>
Suppose BX and CY intersect at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>.</mo><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, so obtained is the given triangle.
(iii) Draw a ray BZ making an acute angle with BC on opposite side of vertex A with respect to BC .
(iv) Draw four (greater of 4 and 3 in 4/3) arcs intersecting the rays BZ at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>.
(v) Join <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> to C and draw a line through <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> parallel to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mi>C</mi></mrow></math>, intersecting the extended line segment BC at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.
(vi) Draw a line through <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> parallel to CA intersecting the extended line segment BA at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.
Triangle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> so obtained is the required triangle.
2. Construct a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math> in which <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>7.5</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>. Now construct a triangle similar to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math> such that each of its sides is third-fourth
of the corresponding sides of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math>. Also prove your assertion.
Sol. Steps of construction :
(i) Draw a line segment <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
(ii) With B as centre and radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, draw an arc.
(iii) With C as centre and radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>7.5</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, draw another arc, intersecting the arc drawn in step (ii) at the point A .
(iv) Join A to B and C to obtain <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
(v) Below BC draw ray BX , making an acute angle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
(vi) Draw four arcs intersecting the ray BX at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>
(vii) Join <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mi>C</mi></mrow></math>.
(viii) Since we have to construct a triangle each of whose sides is third-fourth of the corresponding sides of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math>. Hence draw <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mi>C</mi></mrow></math>.
(ix) From <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>, draw <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, intersecting BA at point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>. Then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> is the required triangle.
3. Construct a triangle similar to a given equilateral <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></mrow></mrow></math> with side 5 cm such that each
of its sides is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">6</mn></mrow></mrow><mrow><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">7</mn></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> th of the corresponding side of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
Sol. Steps of construction :
(i) Draw a line segment <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>
(ii) With Q as centre and radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, draw an arc.
(iii) With R as centre and radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, draw another arc intersecting the arc drawn in step (ii) at the point P .
(iv) Join PQ and PR to obtain <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
(v) Below QR , draw ray QX making an acute angle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
(vi) Draw seven arcs intersecting the ray QX at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>; such that
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>
(vii) Join <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></msub><mi>R</mi></mrow></math>.
(viii) Draw <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></msub><mi>R</mi></mrow></math>, intersecting QR at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>
(ix) From <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> draw <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, intersecting the QP at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.
We get required <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>Q</mi><msup><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> similar to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>Q</mi><mi>R</mi></mrow></math>.
4. Construct a triangle similar to a given triangle ABC with its sides equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">7</mn></mrow></mrow><mrow><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">5</mn></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> th of the corresponding sides of triangle ABC .

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mtable><mtr><mtd columnalign="left" /><mtd columnalign="left"><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="left"><mo>⇒</mo></mtd><mtd columnalign="left"><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>6</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mn>4</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>36</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="left"><mo>∴</mo></mtd><mtd columnalign="left"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>2.236</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>4.5</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mo>.</mo><mtext> (approximate) </mtext></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></math>

5. Steps of construction :
(i) Draw a line segment BC of length 4.3 cm .

(iii) With centre B and radius 2.8 cm draw an arc intersecting the ray BX at A .
(iv) Join A and C.
(v) Draw perpendicular BD from B to AC .
(vi) Draw perpendicular bisector of BC , which bisect BC at piont P .
(vii) With PC as a radius draw a circle which passes through <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></math> and D .

8. To draw tangents on the given circle:
Steps of construction :
(i) Draw a circle of 3 cm radius with centre O .
(ii) Draw a circle of 5 cm radius, taking O as centre. Locate a point P on circle and join OP .
(iii) Bisect OP . Let M be midpoint of OP .
(iv) Taking M as its centre and MO as its radius, draw a circle. Let it intersect the smaller circle at points <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>Q</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>R</mi></mrow></math>.

## Justification:
Since PQ and PR are of lengths 4 cm each.
For <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi></mrow></mrow></math> is tangent at Q .
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mi>&</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>90</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mspace linebreak="newline" /><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mi>&</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mspace linebreak="newline" /><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mi>&</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></math>
By Pythagoras theorem in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow></mrow></math>,
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi>&</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mspace linebreak="newline" /><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi>&</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mspace linebreak="newline" /><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi>&</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>9</mn><mspace linebreak="newline" /><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi>&</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn><mspace linebreak="newline" /><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi></mrow><mi>&</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></math>
Thus justified.

## Steps of construction:
(i) Draw <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math> using SAS rule with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>60</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>
