Sol. Mid-point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>D</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>
Mid-point E <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>
Mid-point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>F</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>
Now, using the formula, area of triangle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">|</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">|</mo></mrow></mrow></math>
⇒ Area of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mi>D</mi><mi>E</mi><mi>F</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></math> square units.
Hence, the area of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mi>D</mi><mi>E</mi><mi>F</mi></mrow></math> is 4 square units.
8. What kind of triangle is formed by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> ?
Sol. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>⇒</mo></mrow></math> it is isosceles.
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>></mo><mi>A</mi><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>B</mi><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>⇒</mo><mn>32</mn><mo>></mo><mn>10</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mo>∠</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow></math> is obtuse
Hence, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi></mrow></math> is an obtuse isosceles <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi></mrow></math>.
9. The area of a triangle is 5 . Two of its vertices are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. The third vertex lies on <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math>. Find the third vertex.
Sol. Let the third vertex be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>, area of triangle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">|</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">[</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">]</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">|</mo></mrow></mrow></math>
As <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>, area of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>⇒</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">|</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">|</mo></mrow></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>⇒</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">|</mo><mn>3</mn><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">|</mo></mrow><mo>⇒</mo><mn>3</mn><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>±</mi><mn>17</mn></mrow></math>
Taking positive sign, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>3</mn><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mn>3</mn><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>17</mn></mrow></math>
Taking negative sign, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>3</mn><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mn>3</mn><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math>
Given that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> lies on <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math>
So, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math>
Solving eqs. (i) and (iii), <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>13</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>
Solving eqs. (ii) and (iii), <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mspace width="1em" /><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mspace width="1em" /><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>.
So the third vertex is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>13</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> or <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>
10. Find the co-ordinates of points which trisect the line segment joining <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>.
Sol. Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> be the given points and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mi>&</mi><mi>D</mi></mrow></math> be the points of trisection.
Then, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∴</mo><mspace width="1em" /><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>p</mi></mrow></math>
and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>p</mi></mrow></math>
then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mi>:</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi><mi>:</mi><mn>2</mn><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>:</mi><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>
and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi></mrow><mi>:</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>p</mi><mi>:</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>:</mi><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>
Let C divides AB internally in the ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mi>:</mi><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> while D divides it in the ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>:</mi><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>.
∴ By section formula, we have
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>&</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">[</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mtext> and </mtext><mspace linebreak="newline" /><mi>&</mi><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">[</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math>
Hence, the two points of trisection are C and D .

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>&</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>Q</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msqrt><mtext> units </mtext><mspace linebreak="newline" /><mi>&</mi><mi>Q</mi><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>0</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>16</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msqrt><mtext> units </mtext><mspace linebreak="newline" /><mi>&</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msqrt><mtext> units </mtext></mrow></mrow></math>
Now, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>Q</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>R</mi><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> units <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msqrt></mrow></math> units <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>Q</mi><mi>R</mi></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∴</mo><mspace width="1em" /><mi>P</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Q</mi></mrow></math>, and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>R</mi></mrow></math> are collinear points.

or, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>α</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>α</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>β</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>13</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>α</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>β</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>α</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow></math>
Subtracting <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>α</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> from each, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>α</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>β</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>13</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>β</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow></math>
From the first two, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>8</mn><mi>α</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>β</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>
From the last two, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>β</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>
Solving (ii) and (iii) we get <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∴</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo></mrow></math> circumcentre.
Now, radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>25</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>25</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>50</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>
14. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>,</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> are middle points of the sides of a triangle, find its incentre.
Sol. Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> be vertices of a triangle, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>,
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>,
on solving these, we get <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>
Now,
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msqrt><mspace width="1em" /><mi>C</mi><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>
∴ Incentre of a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>
15. Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> be the vertices of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi></mrow></math>.
If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> are the vertices of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, find the coordinates of the centroid of the triangle.
Sol. Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> be the vertices of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math> whose medians are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi></mrow></mrow></math> and CF respectively. So, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>E</mi></mrow></math> and F are respectively the mid-points of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow></mrow></math> and AB .
Coordinates of D are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>.
Coordinates of a point dividing AD in the ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>:</mi><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> are
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>
The coordinates of E are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>. The coordinates of a point dividing BE in the ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>:</mi><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>
Similarly, the coordinates of a point dividing CF in the ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>:</mi><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> are
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>
Thus, the point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> is common to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi></mrow></mrow></math> and CF and divides them in the ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>:</mi><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>.
∴ The medians of a triangle are concurrent and the coordinates of the centroid are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>.
## Multiple Choice Questions
DIRECTIONS : This section contains multiple choice questions. Each question has 4 choices (a), (b), (c) and (d) out of which only one is correct.
1. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>13</mn></mrow></math>, what is the value of ' <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> '?
(a) 5
(b 3
(c) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mspace width="1em" /><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math>
(d) -5

rows.question: If the bearing from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi></mrow></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>E</mi><msup><mn>30</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mi>S</mi></mrow></math>, then find the bearing from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi></mrow></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow></math> from North to West direction.
rows.answer:
Since, the bearing from A to B is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>E</mi><msup><mn>30</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mi>S</mi></mrow></math> means <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mn>30</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math> from East to South.
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∴</mo><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>30</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math>
Now, we have to find the bearing from B to A from North to West direction.
i.e. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo></mrow></math> ?
Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></math>.
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">W</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>30</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math> [Alternate interior angles]
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∵</mo><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">W</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>90</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∴</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>30</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>90</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>◻</mi><mo>⇒</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>90</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mn>30</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>60</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math>
Thus, the bearing from B to A from North to West direction is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mn>60</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.

rows.title: ILLUSTRATION : 1
rows.question: If the bearing from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi></mrow></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>E</mi><msup><mn>30</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mi>S</mi></mrow></math>, then find the bearing from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi></mrow></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow></math> from North to West direction.
rows.answer:
Since, the bearing from A to B is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>E</mi><msup><mn>30</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mi>S</mi></mrow></math> means <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mn>30</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math> from East to South.
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∴</mo><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>30</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math>
Now, we have to find the bearing from B to A from North to West direction.
i.e. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo></mrow></math> ?
Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></math>.
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">W</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>30</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math> [Alternate interior angles]
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∵</mo><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">W</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>90</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∴</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>30</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>90</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>◻</mi><mo>⇒</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>90</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mn>30</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>60</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math>
Thus, the bearing from B to A from North to West direction is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mn>60</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.

(iv) Join B to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>.
(v) Through <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> draw a line <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> parallel to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow></mrow></math> by making <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> equal

The point P so obtained is the required point, which divides AB internally in the ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>:</mi><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>.
## Alternative Method for Division of a Line Segment Internally in a Given Ratio
Use the following steps to divide a given line segment AB internally in a given ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>:</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> are natural numbers.

(ii) Draw a ray AX making a suitable acute angle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></mrow></mrow></math> with AB .

(iv) Draw arcs intersecting the ray AX at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, and ray BY at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> such that
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>B</mi><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math>

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>120</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mo>∴</mo><mspace width="1em" /><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>120</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>

Required : To draw the tangent to the circle at P .
Steps of construction :
(i) Take a point O as centre and draw a circle of given radius.
(ii) Take a point P on the circle.
(iii) Join OP.
(iv) Draw a line AB perpendicular to OP at the point P . Line APB is the required tangent at P .

Case (b) : To draw the tangent to a circle at a given point on it, when the centre of the circle is
not known.
Given : A circle and a point P on it.

Steps of construction :
(i) Draw any chord PQ through P and join P and Q to a point R in major <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>arc</mo><mover><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>⏜</mo></mover></mrow></math> (or minor <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>arc</mo><mover><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>⏜</mo></mover></mrow></math> ).

Produce BP to A to get the required tangent APB

## CONSTRUCTION OF TANGENTS TO A CIRCLE FROM A POINT OUTSIDE THE CIRCLE
In this situation, when the point lies outside the circle, there will be two tangents to the circle from this point.
In this construction, again we have two different situations:
Case (a) : To draw the tangents to a circle from a point outside it (external point), when its centre is known.
Given : A circle with centre O and a point P outside it.
Required : To construct the tangents to the circle from point P .
Steps of construction :
(i) Join OP and bisect it. Let M be the mid-point of OP .
(ii) Taking M as centre and MO as radius, draw a circle which intersect the given circle in two points, say A and B .
(iii) Join P to A and P to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>.</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow></mrow></math> and PB are the required tangents from P to given circle .

rows.title: ILLUSTRATION : <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">6</mn></mrow></mrow></math>
rows.question: Draw a circle of radius 2.5 cm . From a point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>. apart from the centre of the circle, draw two tangents to the circle.
rows.answer:
Given : A point P is at a distance of 6 cm . from the centre of a circle with radius 2.5 cm .
Required : To draw two tangents to the circle from the given point P .
Steps of construction :
(i) Draw a line segment OP of length 6 cm .
(ii) With centre O and radius equal to 2.5 cm , draw a circle.
(iii) Draw the right bisector of OP , which intersects OP at M .
(iv) Taking M as centre and MO as radius, draw a circle, which intersect the given circle in two points, say A and B .
(v) Join PA and PB . These are the required tangents from P to the given circle.
Case (b): To draw the tangents to a circle from a point outside it (external point), when its centre is not known.
Given : A circle and a point P outside it.
Required : To construct the tangents to the circle from point P .
Step of construction :
(i) Through <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> draw a secant <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi></mrow></math>, which intersects the circle at points <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi></mrow></math> (say).
(ii) Produce <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> to a point C such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>P</mi><mi>C</mi></mrow></math> i.e., <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> is the mid-point of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>C</mi></mrow></math>.
(iii) Draw a semi-circle with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi></mrow></math> as diameter.
(iv) Draw <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>D</mi><mi>⟂</mi><mi>C</mi><mi>B</mi></mrow></math>, which intersects the semi-circle at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>D</mi></mrow></math>.
(v) With <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> as centre and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>D</mi></mrow></math> as radius draw arcs to intersect the given circle at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>T</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.
(vi) Join P to T and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>. Then PT and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> are the required tangents.

rows.answer:
Given : A circle with radius 4 cm and a point P outside it.
Required : To draw two tangents to the circle from the given point P .

(i) Draw a circle of radius 4 cm .
(ii) Take a point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> outside the circle and draw a secant <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi></mrow></math>, which intersects the circle at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi></mrow></math>.
(iii) Produce <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi></mrow></math> such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>C</mi><mi>P</mi></mrow></math>.
(iv) Draw a semi-circle with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mi>B</mi></mrow></math> as diameter.
(v) Draw <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>D</mi><mi>⟂</mi><mi>C</mi><mi>B</mi></mrow></math>, which intersects the semi-circle at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>D</mi></mrow></math>.
(vi) With <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> as centre and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>D</mi></mrow></math> as radius draw arcs to intersect the given circle at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>T</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.
(vii) Join <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>T</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>. Then, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>T</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><msup><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> are the required tangents.

(v) Join <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> to C and draw a line through <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> parallel to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mi>C</mi></mrow></math>, intersecting the extended line segment BC at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.
(vi) Draw a line through <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> parallel to CA intersecting the extended line segment BA at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.
Triangle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> so obtained is the required triangle.
2. Construct a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math> in which <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>7.5</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>. Now construct a triangle similar to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math> such that each of its sides is third-fourth
of the corresponding sides of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math>. Also prove your assertion.
Sol. Steps of construction :
(i) Draw a line segment <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
(ii) With B as centre and radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, draw an arc.
(iii) With C as centre and radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>7.5</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, draw another arc, intersecting the arc drawn in step (ii) at the point A .
(iv) Join A to B and C to obtain <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
(v) Below BC draw ray BX , making an acute angle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
(vi) Draw four arcs intersecting the ray BX at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>
(vii) Join <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mi>C</mi></mrow></math>.
(viii) Since we have to construct a triangle each of whose sides is third-fourth of the corresponding sides of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math>. Hence draw <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mi>C</mi></mrow></math>.
(ix) From <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>, draw <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, intersecting BA at point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>. Then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> is the required triangle.
3. Construct a triangle similar to a given equilateral <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></mrow></mrow></math> with side 5 cm such that each
of its sides is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">6</mn></mrow></mrow><mrow><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">7</mn></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> th of the corresponding side of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
Sol. Steps of construction :
(i) Draw a line segment <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>
(ii) With Q as centre and radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, draw an arc.
(iii) With R as centre and radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, draw another arc intersecting the arc drawn in step (ii) at the point P .
(iv) Join PQ and PR to obtain <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
(v) Below QR , draw ray QX making an acute angle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
(vi) Draw seven arcs intersecting the ray QX at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>; such that
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>…</mi><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>
(vii) Join <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></msub><mi>R</mi></mrow></math>.
(viii) Draw <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></msub><mi>R</mi></mrow></math>, intersecting QR at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>
(ix) From <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> draw <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, intersecting the QP at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.
We get required <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>Q</mi><msup><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> similar to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>Q</mi><mi>R</mi></mrow></math>.
4. Construct a triangle similar to a given triangle ABC with its sides equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">7</mn></mrow></mrow><mrow><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">5</mn></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> th of the corresponding sides of triangle ABC .
Sol. Steps of construction :
(i) Draw a ray BX making a suitable acute angle with BC on opposite side of A.
(ii) Draw seven arcs intersecting the ray BX at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mi>…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>
(iii) Join <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> to C and draw a line <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> parallel to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub><mi>C</mi></mrow></math>, which intersects BC producted at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.
(iv) Draw a line <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> parallel to CA to intersect BA producted at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>. Then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>Δ</mi><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> will be the required triangle.
5. Construct a triangle ABC whose sides are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>7.5</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math> and 6.5 cm . Construct a triangle similar to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math> with sides <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">2</mn></mrow></mrow><mrow><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">3</mn></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">r</mi><mi mathvariant="bold">d</mi></mrow></mrow></math> of the corresponding sides of triangle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">A</mi><mi mathvariant="bold">B</mi><mi mathvariant="bold">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
Sol. Steps of construction :
(i) Take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>7.5</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>. With B as centre and radius 7 cm draw an arc.
(ii) With C as centre and radius 6.5 cm , draw arc intersecting the arc drawn in step (i) at point A . Then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>△</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mrow></math> is the required triangle.
(iii) Draw a ray BX making an acute angle with BC opposite side of A with respect to BC .
(iv) Draw three arcs intersecting the ray BX at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>.
(v) Join <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mi>C</mi></mrow></math>.
(vi) Draw <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mi>C</mi></mrow></math>, which intersects BC at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.
(vii) Draw <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, which intersects BA at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>. ## Alternative Method for Division of a Line Segment Internally in a Given Ratio

## CONSTRUCTION OF A TRIANGLE SIMILAR TO A GIVEN TRIANGLE (AS PER GIVEN SCALE FACTOR)
## Scale Factor

Triangle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> so obtained is the required triangle.

## To construct an equilateral triangle circumscribed over a circle of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">r</mi></mrow><mrow><mtext mathvariant="bold"> </mtext><mi mathvariant="bold">c</mi><mi mathvariant="bold">m</mi></mrow></mrow></math>.
## Steps of Construction

Step 2: Draw radii OP, OQ and OR such that
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>120</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mo>∴</mo><mspace width="1em" /><mo>∠</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>120</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>
