## TRANSPOSE OF A MATRIX
If the rows and corresponding columns of a matrix <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow></math> of order <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>×</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> are interchanged, we get a new matrix of the order <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>×</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow></math>, which is called the transpose of the matrix <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow></math>. The transpose of a matrix <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow></math> is denoted by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> or <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>. For example:
If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">[</mo><mtable><mtr><mtd columnalign="center"><mn>1</mn></mtd><mtd columnalign="center"><mn>7</mn></mtd><mtd columnalign="center"><mn>2</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="center"><mn>2</mn></mtd><mtd columnalign="center"><mn>5</mn></mtd><mtd columnalign="center"><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="center"><mn>3</mn></mtd><mtd columnalign="center"><mn>4</mn></mtd><mtd columnalign="center"><mn>1</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">]</mo></mrow></mrow></math>, then the transpose of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow></math> can be expressed as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">[</mo><mtable><mtr><mtd columnalign="center"><mn>1</mn></mtd><mtd columnalign="center"><mn>2</mn></mtd><mtd columnalign="center"><mn>3</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="center"><mn>7</mn></mtd><mtd columnalign="center"><mn>5</mn></mtd><mtd columnalign="center"><mn>4</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="center"><mn>2</mn></mtd><mtd columnalign="center"><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mtd><mtd columnalign="center"><mn>1</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">]</mo></mrow></mrow></math>
## Properties of Transpose of a Matrix
(i) The transpose of the sum of two matrices is the sum of their transpose, i.e., <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>B</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.
(ii) The transpose of the transpose of a matrix is the matrix itself, i.e., <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow></math>.
(iii) If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow></math> is a matrix of any order and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow></math> is a scalar, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mi>A</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.
(iv) The transpose of the product of two matrices is the product in reverse order of their transpose, i.e., <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.

A square matrix <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">[</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> is called symmetric if <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, for all values of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>i</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>j</mi></mrow></math>.
